questions.q: Which Harappan site is known for its ancient dockyard, indicating maritime trade?
questions.solution:
**Lothal** (Gujarat) has a brick-built dockyard, pointing to sea trade with Mesopotamia. Kalibangan is known for ploughed fields and fire altars, and Rakhigarhi is one of the largest Indus sites.

**Answer: Lothal**
questions.shortcut: Lothal = 'place of the dead', but its fame is the dock — think 'boat-lothal'.

questions.q: Which Gupta ruler assumed the celebrated title 'Vikramaditya'?
questions.solution:
**Chandragupta II** took the title Vikramaditya ('sun of valour') after victories over the Shakas (west Kshatrapas). His court hosted the navaratnas, including Kalidasa.

**Answer: Chandragupta II**
questions.shortcut: Vikramaditya = Shakari, the 'Shaka-destroyer' → Chandragupta II.

questions.q: The Battle of Talikota (1565) resulted in the decisive defeat of which empire?
questions.solution:
At **Talikota (1565)** a combined army of the Deccan Sultanates crushed the **Vijayanagara Empire**, which never fully recovered; the city was sacked and the glory days ended.

**Answer: Vijayanagara Empire**
questions.shortcut: 1565 → Talikota → fall of Hampi/Vijayanagara.

questions.q: The Partition of Bengal, which triggered the Swadeshi Movement, was carried out in 1905 during the viceroyalty of:
questions.solution:
The Partition of Bengal (announced in July 1905, effective October 1905) was carried out by **Lord Curzon**; it was annulled in 1911 under Lord Hardinge. Ripon is remembered for the Ilbert Bill and local self-government.

**Answer: Lord Curzon**
questions.shortcut: 1905 partition → Curzon; 1911 annulment → Hardinge.

questions.q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 1919 took place in Amritsar on which occasion?
questions.solution:
The firing ordered by General Dyer fell on **Baisakhi**, 13 April 1919, when a large crowd had gathered at Jallianwala Bagh after the parade.

**Answer: Baisakhi**
questions.shortcut: 13 April = Baisakhi = Jallianwala Bagh.

questions.q: The Simon Commission was boycotted by Indian political parties primarily because:
options: it recommended the partition of Bengal
it was headed by a British civil servant
it proposed fresh taxes on Indians
questions.solution:
All seven members of the Simon Commission (1928) were **British — no Indian was included** — so parties across the spectrum boycotted it with 'Simon Go Back' demonstrations.

**Answer: it had no Indian member**
questions.shortcut: Boycott slogan's root: 'all-white' commission.

questions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution gives every citizen the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
questions.solution:
**Article 32** — the Right to Constitutional Remedies — lets citizens approach the Supreme Court directly, and Dr Ambedkar called it the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution. Article 226 is the wider writ power of the High Courts.

**Answer: Article 32**
questions.shortcut: 32 = the 'remedy' article — heart and soul (Ambedkar).

questions.q: Who acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.solution:
Under Article 64 the **Vice President** is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha; the Deputy Chairman presides in the Vice President's absence.

**Answer: The Vice President**
questions.shortcut: RS has no elected Speaker → the Vice President anchors it.

questions.q: Under the Constitution of India, who is the Supreme Commander of the Defence Forces?
questions.solution:
Article 53(2) vests the supreme command of the Armed Forces in the **President of India**, exercised on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.

**Answer: The President**
questions.shortcut: Defence forces take orders in the President's name.

questions.q: Which of the following is no longer a Fundamental Right under the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The **Right to Property** was dropped from Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment (1978) and made a legal right under Article 300A. The other three remain Fundamental Rights.

**Answer: Right to Property**
questions.shortcut: 44th Amendment (1978): property out of Part III → into 300A.

questions.q: Which is the highest mountain peak lying entirely within Indian territory?
questions.solution:
**Nanda Devi** (7,816 m, Uttarakhand) is the highest peak entirely inside India. Kanchenjunga stands on the India–Nepal border and K2 lies in Pakistan-occupied territory.

**Answer: Nanda Devi**
questions.shortcut: Border peaks (K2, Kanchenjunga) are out; 'entirely inside' → Nanda Devi.

questions.q: Chilika Lake, the largest brackish-water lagoon of India, lies in which state?
questions.solution:
**Chilika** is in **Odisha** and is famous for migratory birds and Irrawaddy dolphins. Pulicat lagoon lies in Andhra Pradesh and the Vembanad backwaters in Kerala.

**Answer: Odisha**
questions.shortcut: Chilika–Odisha, Pulicat–Andhra, Vembanad–Kerala.

questions.q: Which is the largest hot desert of the world?
questions.solution:
The **Sahara** (North Africa) is the largest hot desert, covering an area comparable to that of the United States. The Gobi is a cold desert in Asia.

**Answer: Sahara**
questions.shortcut: Largest overall = Antarctic; largest hot = Sahara.

questions.q: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) guarantees how many days of wage employment per rural household in a financial year?
questions.solution:
MGNREGA (2005, in force from February 2006) guarantees **100 days** of unskilled wage employment per rural household per financial year; unemployment allowance is payable if work is not given.

**Answer: 100 days**
questions.shortcut: Employment guarantee = the 100-day Act.

questions.q: NITI Aayog, which replaced the Planning Commission, was established on:
questions.solution:
The Planning Commission was replaced by **NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015**, with the Prime Minister as its Chairperson.

**Answer: 1 January 2015**
questions.shortcut: New year, new think tank: 1 Jan 2015.

questions.q: Sound waves cannot travel through:
questions.solution:
Sound needs a material medium (solid, liquid or gas) to propagate, so it cannot travel through a **vacuum** — space is silent. Steel, water and air all conduct sound, solids being the fastest.

**Answer: vacuum**
questions.shortcut: Bell in a jar experiment: pump out air → no sound.

questions.q: Which device converts mechanical energy into electrical energy?
questions.solution:
An **electric generator** (dynamo) converts mechanical energy into electrical energy using electromagnetic induction; the motor does the exact reverse.

**Answer: Electric generator**
questions.shortcut: generator = makes electricity; motor = uses electricity.

questions.q: The characteristic smell of rotten eggs is due to which gas?
questions.solution:
**Hydrogen sulphide (H2S)** gives rotten eggs their smell. Ammonia has a sharp pungent odour, carbon monoxide is odourless and sulphur dioxide smells like burnt matchsticks.

**Answer: Hydrogen sulphide**
questions.shortcut: S + H → H2S = rotten egg; SO2 = burnt match.

questions.q: What is the pH value of a neutral solution at 25 °C?
questions.solution:
A neutral solution (equal H+ and OH–) has **pH 7** at 25 °C; below 7 is acidic and above 7 is basic. Pure water is the classic example.

**Answer: 7**
questions.shortcut: pH 7 = neutral, < 7 acid, > 7 base.

questions.q: Which organelle of the cell is called the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
questions.solution:
**Mitochondria** release energy from food as ATP through cellular respiration, earning the name 'powerhouse of the cell'. Ribosomes make proteins and the Golgi apparatus packages them.

**Answer: Mitochondria**
questions.shortcut: Powerhouse = ATP factory = mitochondria.

questions.q: Which blood group is regarded as the universal donor?
questions.solution:
**O negative** blood has no A, B antigens or Rh(D) antigen, so it can be given to almost any patient in an emergency. AB positive, with all antigens, is the universal recipient.

**Answer: O negative**
questions.shortcut: O = 'zero' antigens → donates to all; AB+ accepts all.

questions.q: In plants, water and minerals absorbed by the roots are transported upward to the leaves through:
questions.solution:
**Xylem** carries water and dissolved minerals upward from roots to leaves; phloem transports prepared food in both directions.

**Answer: Xylem**
questions.shortcut: Xylem = up (water); phloem = food both ways.

questions.q: Which is the largest state of India by area?
questions.solution:
**Rajasthan** (about 3.42 lakh sq km) is India's largest state by area, followed by Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.

**Answer: Rajasthan**
questions.shortcut: Area 1-2-3: Rajasthan, MP, Maharashtra.

questions.q: Who is the author of the famous Hindi novel 'Godan'?
questions.solution:
'**Godan**' (1936), the story of the poor farmer Hori, was written by **Munshi Premchand**. Bankim Chandra wrote 'Anandamath' and Sarat Chandra wrote 'Devdas'.

**Answer: Munshi Premchand**
questions.shortcut: Godan = gift of a cow → Premchand's peasant classic.

questions.q: Which team won the ICC Men's Champions Trophy 2025, defeating New Zealand in the final?
questions.solution:
**India** beat New Zealand in the final of the ICC Men's Champions Trophy 2025, played at Dubai in March 2025, to lift the title.

**Answer: India**
questions.shortcut: 2025 Champions Trophy → India (Dubai final).
